title: Passing Yards Speed Step 7 Same-Session Full Analysis Transition
objective: Measure and remove the remaining user-visible delay caused by the lazy-shell Load Full Analysis transition, without changing any frozen football/model/data/projection/context/probability/market/sportsbook behavior.
current_first_broken_arrow: Lazy shell -> Load Full Analysis -> selected-QB full detail ready
diagnostic_action: One branch browser profile proving whether the current V79 Load Full Analysis anchor causes a full document navigation and measuring click-to-ready versus frozen V77 server-render telemetry.

current_failure_epoch.root_cause: V83 uses a normal Streamlit button event (which already reruns the app) and then calls st.rerun() explicitly after setting ks_py_full=1. Production therefore pays for an avoidable second rerun/roundtrip. Local branch latency masked the transport penalty; public wrapper telemetry proves the extra transport cost.
current_failure_epoch.patch: V84 single-rerun transport: set ks_py_full=1 in the button on_click callback and remove the explicit second st.rerun. The button's native rerun renders the unchanged V83/V82 full-analysis descendant.

root_cause.conclusion: Legacy V79 Load Full Analysis anchor is sanitized/rendered with target=_blank. The current Streamlit document remains on the lazy URL, so ks_py_full=1 never activates in the existing session.

product_patch.description: Single-rerun same-session activation using Streamlit on_click callback. No football/model/data/projection/context/probability/market/sportsbook changes.

navigation_change_scope: Transport scheduling only: ks_py_full=1 is set in the button callback before the native Streamlit rerun; no explicit second rerun.
acceptance_gates: 1 root cause locked from live public wrapper telemetry
4 branch single-rerun browser proof GREEN with V82-wrapper transport <=1.5s
9 public single-rerun proof preserves Step6 <=24s ready ceiling and V82-wrapper transport overhead <=1.5s, with Step6 prefetch/payload contracts preserved
10 successful public job emits PASSING_YARDS_SPEED_STEP7_GREEN + PASSING_YARDS_SPEED_STEP7_FROZEN
next_required_state: Timing-verifier-only PR GREEN -> merge -> public immediate-DOM timing proof -> PASSING_YARDS_SPEED_STEP7_GREEN + FROZEN

current_public_reclassification.conclusion: Public Streamlit activated V84 and exited the lazy shell in the same document, but the browser URL did not retain ks_py_full=1. URL persistence is not a Step 7 acceptance gate. Reclassify the failure as verifier-only and prove the selected-QB full-detail DOM plus the frozen latency/prefetch/payload contracts directly.
current_public_reclassification.patch: Verifier-only: keep same-document proof, treat URL flag visibility as telemetry, require full-detail DOM readiness, then enforce <=24s click-to-ready, <=1.5s V82-wrapper transport overhead, prefetch hits/fallbacks, and payload ceiling. Product V84/V235 remains unchanged.

current_timing_reclassification.root_cause: The public verifier waited up to 12 seconds for ks_py_full=1 to appear in page.url before looking for the full-detail DOM, then included that URL synchronization wait inside click_ready_seconds. The measured 12.194s therefore does not represent detail readiness; subtracting the 5.175s wrapper time produces an artificial 7.019s transport overhead.
current_timing_reclassification.patch: Verifier-only timing repair: start the full-detail selector wait immediately after button.click(), capture click_ready_seconds as soon as the selected-QB detail DOM is ready, then sample URL visibility and same-document state as telemetry. Keep all existing <=24s, <=1.5s, prefetch/fallback, payload, and identity gates unchanged.
